03-who.title: WHO's fact sheets end in a stray semicolon.
03-who.linkedin:
WHO's fact sheets end in a stray semicolon.

WHO welcomes AI answer crawlers and its pages read well without JavaScript: GEO 91. But the JSON-LD on its fact sheets ends in "};", and a strict parser drops the whole block.

The lesson for every team: Run every JSON-LD block through a JSON validator before release. One character can void the entire block.

04-govco.title: GOV.CO is empty until JavaScript runs.
04-govco.linkedin:
GOV.CO is empty until JavaScript runs.

The portal for more than 78,000 government procedures sends an HTML body with almost no text. Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript, so they see a title and little else.

The lesson for every team: Render the main text on the server, or prerender the start page. View source should show what a visitor reads.

One automated read of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

DMARC reject, preloaded HSTS, and Core Web Vitals that pass for real visitors. Its robots.txt also turns away AI answer crawlers like ChatGPT search and Perplexity. GEO: 56.

The lesson for every team: Blocking AI training and blocking AI answers are separate choices. Name each crawler in robots.txt on purpose.

08-bancolombia.title: Bancolombia's site won't let you zoom.
08-bancolombia.linkedin:
Bancolombia's site won't let you zoom.

Language versions link to each other, share cards are complete, and pages read without JavaScript. But the viewport sets maximum-scale=1, which blocks pinch-zoom on many phones for people who need larger text.

The lesson for every team: Drop maximum-scale and user-scalable=no from your viewport tag. Zoom is how many people read.

One automated read of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

09-un.title: The UN home page never says its language.
09-un.linkedin:
The UN home page never says its language.

Links answer, campaign tags survive redirects, and AI answer crawlers are welcome. But the start page's <html> tag has no lang, so screen readers guess the voice and browsers guess the translation.

The lesson for every team: Put lang on the html tag of every language version: lang="en", lang="fr", lang="ar". One attribute per page.

One automated read of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.
